title: Build an inventory management service: CRUD, search, low-stock alerts, export
description: Multi-step Python task: implement an in-memory inventory service with CRUD, then add search and filtering, then add low-stock alerts, then add CSV export. Tests are injected.

injections.content:
[project]
name = "python-inventory"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = ["pytest>=8.0", "ruff>=0.4"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["src"]
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100

import pytest
from inventory import Inventory


# Step 1: CRUD
def test_add_and_get():
    inv = Inventory()
    item_id = inv.add(name="Widget", quantity=10, price=2.50)
    item = inv.get(item_id)
    assert item["name"] == "Widget"
    assert item["quantity"] == 10
    assert abs(item["price"] - 2.50) < 0.001


def test_get_missing():
    inv = Inventory()
    assert inv.get(9999) is None


def test_update_quantity():
    inv = Inventory()
    item_id = inv.add("Gadget", 5, 9.99)
    inv.update(item_id, quantity=20)
    assert inv.get(item_id)["quantity"] == 20


def test_delete():
    inv = Inventory()
    item_id = inv.add("Thingy", 1, 1.00)
    assert inv.delete(item_id) is True
    assert inv.get(item_id) is None


def test_delete_missing():
    inv = Inventory()
    assert inv.delete(999) is False


# Step 2: Search and filtering
def test_search_by_name():
    inv = Inventory()
    inv.add("Apple", 100, 0.5)
    inv.add("Banana", 50, 0.3)
    inv.add("Apricot", 20, 0.8)
    results = inv.search("ap")
    names = [r["name"] for r in results]
    assert "Apple" in names
    assert "Apricot" in names
    assert "Banana" not in names


def test_filter_by_max_price():
    inv = Inventory()
    inv.add("Cheap", 10, 1.0)
    inv.add("Expensive", 5, 100.0)
    results = inv.filter(max_price=10.0)
    assert len(results) == 1
    assert results[0]["name"] == "Cheap"


# Step 3: Low-stock alerts
def test_low_stock_default_threshold():
    inv = Inventory()
    inv.add("Low", 3, 1.0)
    inv.add("Ok", 20, 1.0)
    alerts = inv.low_stock()
    names = [a["name"] for a in alerts]
    assert "Low" in names
    assert "Ok" not in names


def test_low_stock_custom_threshold():
    inv = Inventory()
    inv.add("Item", 15, 1.0)
    assert len(inv.low_stock(threshold=20)) == 1
    assert len(inv.low_stock(threshold=10)) == 0


# Step 4: CSV export
def test_export_csv():
    inv = Inventory()
    inv.add("Bolt", 100, 0.10)
    inv.add("Nut", 200, 0.05)
    csv_text = inv.export_csv()
    lines = csv_text.strip().split("\n")
    assert lines[0] == "id,name,quantity,price"
    assert len(lines) == 3  # header + 2 items
    assert "Bolt" in csv_text

task_spec.prompt:
Create src/inventory.py implementing a 4-step inventory management service.

Step 1 — CRUD:
  class Inventory:
    add(name: str, quantity: int, price: float) -> int  # returns new item ID
    get(item_id: int) -> dict | None
    update(item_id: int, *, quantity: int | None = None, price: float | None = None) -> bool
    delete(item_id: int) -> bool

Step 2 — Search and filtering:
    search(query: str) -> list[dict]  # case-insensitive substring match on name
    filter(*, max_price: float | None = None, min_quantity: int | None = None) -> list[dict]

Step 3 — Low-stock alerts:
    low_stock(threshold: int = 10) -> list[dict]  # items with quantity < threshold

Step 4 — CSV export:
    export_csv() -> str  # header: id,name,quantity,price; one row per item

All 11 tests in tests/test_inventory.py must pass.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
success_criteria: uv run pytest tests/ passes (11 tests)
uv run ruff check src/ passes
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
